THIS WRIT PETITION (CIVIL) HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 07.03.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 W.P.(C.) No. 13271 of 2024  3  2025:KER:21273  T.R. RAVI., J.
 ------------------------------------
 W.P.(C.) No. 13271 of 2024  --------------------------------------
 Dated this the 7th day of March, 2025  JUDGMENT

The petitioner has approached this Court stating that additional extent was sought to be taken possession of, over and above the land acquired and for which the compensation has been paid as per Exts.P2 and P4 awards.
According to the petitioner, an additional extent of land where the petitioner had re-constructed his building
is sought to be acquired and the building is sought to be demolished.
2. A counter affidavit has been filed by the respondents, wherein it is specifically stated that the State has not acquired any portion over and above the lands covered by Exts.P2 and P4 awards.
What is stated is that a total extent of 0.465 Hectares was acquired, of which 0.0020 Hectares is remaining in the possession of the petitioner even though he has already been paid the compensation.

For the apprehension of the petitioner that additional land is being taken possession of without following the procedure under land acquisition Act, the statement filed by the counsel 2025:KER:21273 for the respondents 1,2,4 and 5 and the counter affidavit filed by the State is Karunakaran.
K.R vs Union Of India on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107463439/
2 sufficient answer.
The submission that the State does not intend to acquire any property over and above the property for which the compensation has been paid as per Exts.P2 and P4 awards is recorded.
If the petitioner has any case that additional land has been acquired or taken possession of, it is for the petitioner to establish the same in a competent civil court after letting in evidence.
The respondents are directed to demarcate the property which has been taken possession of from the petitioner.
The respondents shall clearly demarcate the property which has been taken possession of from the petitioner, so that the petitioner can, if he has any grievance, approach the appropriate civil court.
Such demarcation shall be done within one month from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
The writ petition is disposed of as above.
